According to the police report, the three kilogram packages recovered under the driver's side seat field tested positive for cocaine and fentanyl. Erazzo Velazquez, the driver of the vehicle, was charged with trafficking controlled substances, possession with intent to deliver over 900 grams of fentanyl, aggravated fleeing and eluding, and resisting a peace officer. During a search not caught on camera, officers found him in possession of $1,460, which was seized under the Controlled Substances Act. He is currently at Grundy County Jail awaiting trial. He was not released due to the Department of Homeland Security having an immigration detainer warrant against him for being a Honduran national who entered the country illegally. Barahona, the passenger, was charged with trafficking-controlled substances, possession with intent to deliver fentanyl over 900 grams, obstructing justice, and resisting a peace officer. The arresting officer conducted an inquiry through the law enforcement agency's data system and found that Barahona was a missing person from California's Valley Teen Ranch. However, because he had no prior criminal history, Barahona was released from jail with a date to appear in court, in accordance with the Illinois Safety Act. Afterwards, California authorities informed Grundy County that Barahona did indeed have a juvenile record, and that he was also a Honduran national who entered the country illegally, information that would have allowed for his pretrial detention. However, by the time this information was shared with Grundy County, Barahona had already fled the state.
